response.query: LinkedIn User Agreement prohibits automating account access without consent

results.title: Automated activity on LinkedIn | LinkedIn Help
results.snippet: Third-party software that automates tasks could potentially export or scrape data from LinkedIn and affects authenticity; at times, without your consent. This is a violation of LinkedIn’s User Agreement, and may be a violation of privacy legislation in specific jurisdictions.

results.title: User Agreement | LinkedIn
results.snippet: Rent, lease, loan, trade, sell/re-sell or otherwise monetize the Services or related data or access to the same, without LinkedIn’s consent; Deep-link to our Services for any purpose other than to promote your profile or a Group on our Services, without LinkedIn’s consent; Use bots or other unauthorized automated methods to access the Services, add or download contacts, send or redirect messages, create, comment on, like, share, or re-share posts, or otherwise drive inauthentic engagement;

results.title: Prohibited software and extensions | LinkedIn Help
results.snippet: Any member who uses tools for such purposes is in violation of the User Agreement. This means that they risk having their accounts restricted or shut down. They also risk the possibility that any prohibited tools they’re using may become non-operational without notice.

results.title: LinkedIn Automation Tools Violate User Agreement | Mike Kunkle posted on the topic | LinkedIn
results.snippet: This section directly prohibits: 🔹Automated direct messages 🔹Automated follow‑ups 🔹Automated InMail sending 🔹Any tool that sends or redirects messages on a user's behalf So I'm curious how these tools are thriving. Unless they're operating through LinkedIn's authorized API partnerships, which would be a different story, but I can't imagine they all are, if LinkedIn calls out automation in the agreement.

results.title: Why LinkedIn Automation Tools Get Your Account Banned (And What to Do Instead)
results.snippet: LinkedIn explicitly prohibits all third-party automation tools under its User Agreement — no exceptions.
